incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée); Regulation of the Guichet Unique under the PACTE Act and Decree No. 2021-1621
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) under the administrative coordination of the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) via Le Guichet Unique
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statutes (Statuts) executed by all shareholders, accompanied by the simplified incorporation form (M0) and supporting exhibits submitted through Le Guichet Unique
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for SARL; if cash contributions are made, at least 20% of cash contributions must be released upon subscription, with the balance payable within five years. Capital must be deposited in an escrow account with a depositary bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations until full registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION: The shareholders and first manager of the SARL, acting via the initial articles of association, resolve as follows: (i) the validity of the subscriptions to share capital and the release of cash contributions into the escrow account are approved; (ii) the registered office is fixed at the address stated in the articles; (iii) [Name] is appointed as Manager for an indefinite term, with full powers to act on the company's behalf; (iv) the Manager is authorized to complete French registration formalities at the Guichet Unique and before the RCS, and to execute all necessary instruments to commence the acquisition-syndicate and buyout objectives. This resolution is effective upon signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (if required by law, e.g., real estate contribution; otherwise private drafting suffices) and all founding shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare French-law-compliant Statuts identifying corporate form, corporate object, registered office, share capital, shareholding distribution, governance, and manager appointment. Ensure all pages are initialed and signed by each shareholder. If any contribution is made in real property, the Statuts must be executed before a notaire; otherwise private signature is valid.
required_dossiers: Identity card or passport of each shareholder
Signed Statuts (original or electronic signatures)
Shareholder declaration of share subscriptions
Statement of nationality, residence, and legal capacity of founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the drafting deficiencies or ask the notaire to revise the Statuts; re-sign required pages and resubmit to the same filing channel without additional statutory penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Cash Contributions into an Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A bank licensed in the French Republic or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary neutralist account or a 'formation' escrow account in the name of the company in formation and wire the subscribed cash capital. Obtain a certificate of deposit issued by the depositary institution, which is required for the registration file. Use correspondent SWIFT or Euro-denominated transfer for syndicated funds to demonstrate the origin.
required_dossiers: Bank KYC documentation for the company in formation and executive shareholders
Escrow instruction letter signed by the depositor
Certificate of the deposit of capital (Attestation de blocage de fonds)
Structured financing or LBO commitment letter showing source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional AML information, provide shareholder, ultimate beneficial owner, and source-of-wealth documentation; otherwise reopen the account in a different bank licensed in France and obtain the substitution certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish a Legal Notice in an Authorized Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A legal announcement gazette (Journal d'annonces légales) authorized for the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the legal announcement containing the draft company name, legal form, registered office address, corporate object, capital amount, manager identity, and the anticipated filing date. Submit the announcement to the approved gazette and secure proof of publication; the publication must occur before filing the registration application.
required_dossiers: Project articles of association or a complete extract
Identities of shareholders and manager
Registered office address and designation order
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette rejects the notice for incomplete information, amend the legal announcement and republish; the prior rejected notice will not prejudice the filing if a clean proof of publication is provided.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Incorporation File to Le Guichet Unique (INPI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Le Guichet Unique for company formalities operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the M0 magnetization form on the online INPI portal and upload the digitalized Statuts, capital deposit certificate, legal notice publication proof, registered office justification, manager and shareholder identity documents, prescribed declaration of beneficial owners, and sworn attribution of the opening of the business. Pay the electronic filing fee via secure payment.
required_dossiers: Completed M0 form
Final Statuts
Capital deposit certificate / attestation from bank
Legal notice publication receipt
Justification of occupation of registered office (e.g., lease, ownership title, host letter)
Identity documents of shareholders and manager
Declaration of the beneficial owner (Déclaration des titulaires effectifs)
Power of attorney if a representative signs for any founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the INPI system issues a non-conformity query, cure the stated omissions or errors notifying the modification, upload corrected documents, and re-submit within the system; the thirty-day publicity schedule restarts from the date of the compliant resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Registration with the Registers of Commerce and Companies (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce compétent for the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Greffe verifies the legality of the filings after receipt through the Guichet Unique, performs substantive control, assigns the registration number (SIREN), and issues the Kbis extract. Once issued, the company may open a definitive bank account and begin commercial operations. Obtain a certified Kbis extract as the prima facie legal identity proof.
required_dossiers: RCS registration application as transmitted by INPI
Proof of INPI filing receipt
All incorporation exhibits generated by the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a rejection or requests a corrective amendment, file a petition for rectification with the Greffe within two weeks, or alternatively appeal to the first president of the competent tribunal de commerce against the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Finalize Post-Incorporation Governance and Statutory Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's internal learning body; Greffe du tribunal de commerce; French Anti-Money Laundering authorities where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first constitutive board meeting and record the resolution in minutes; verify the appointment of the manager and the address of the registered office; open the mandatory corporate bank account, complete the Register of Shares (registre des mouvements de titres) and Register of Financial Pledges; file transparency declarations and, if relevant, UBO declarations; activate the compliance calendar for annual accounts filing.
required_dossiers: Caller's convocation and minutes of the first board meeting
RCS Kbis extract
Statutory registers (share register, transfer register, UBO register)
Certificate of manager appointment and acceptance
Bank account opening confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a governance inconsistency is noticed by the bank or by a third party, hold an extraordinary shareholders' meeting to ratify the acts and rectify the registry; file any amending instrument with the Greffe within one month.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the official portal at https://www.impots.gouv.fr/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French SARL entities obtain SIREN/SIRET and VAT ID (FR followed by SIREN) through mandatory registration with the tax authorities. Non-resident owners may require a fiscal representative. The process involves online submission via guichet-entreprises.fr or impots.gouv.fr, providing legal incorporation documents, registered office address, activity code (NAF/APE), and capital details. Foreign-owned entities follow the same procedure as domestic entities under French law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available in France. However, hybrid mismatch rules apply under the Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD). Specific regimes such as the SISE (Société de Gestion de Patrimoine Immobilier) or holding company regimes may offer tax optimizations, but default is entity-level taxation for SARL.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 85,000 EUR annual turnover threshold for VAT registration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory implementation of electronic invoicing (Factur-X standard) with real-time transmission to tax authorities via APIs. Digital stamping (horodatage) required for all B2B invoices. Non-compliance can result in fines and loss of VAT deduction rights.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to non-EU destinations qualify for 0% VAT rate. Offshore services may qualify under specific conditions if the service is performed outside France and the recipient is non-EU. Proof of export is mandatory, including delivery to a third country or use by non-EU customer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation en Douane - DAU)
Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of payment from foreign customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims lead to full repayment of erroneously zero-rated VAT plus interest, administrative fines up to 5% of the VAT amount, and potential criminal sanctions including imprisonment. Retrospective audits can claw back benefits if documentation is insufficient or export not proven.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), operating within the Eurosystem and under the policy framework of the European Central Bank. Banking supervision is exercised by the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution), an independent authority organically attached to the Banque de France. Foreign-exchange policy, capital-movement oversight and foreign-direct-investment screening are implemented by the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) within the Ministry of Economy and Finance, in co-operation with the Banque de France.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a fully liberalised euro-area jurisdiction: there is no general exchange-control authorisation, no quantitative convertibility limit and no resident/non-resident distinction for current or capital account transactions. The applicable legal framework is the EU free movement of capital (TFEU Art. 63), the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements and the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier, Arts. L151-1 et seq. and L152-1 et seq.). Capital and current account euro flows are fully convertible; profit remittances from a French SARL are freely executable by dividend, share buyback or reserve distribution once the French mandatory legal reserve (5% of annual profits up to 10% of share capital) has been constituted and the gérant/EGM formalities are completed. French withholding tax applies to distributions to non-EU corporate shareholders unless reduced under an applicable tax treaty; EU corporate shareholders benefit from the Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption. The only operational hurdles are statistical and screening-related: (i) French balance-of-payments reporting to the Banque de France applies where the cumulative monthly cross-border transactions of the company with non-residents equal or exceed EUR 750,000; and (ii) investment by a non-EU investor in a French entity requires assessment of the EU/French FDI regime, prior ministerial authorisation being required only for sensitive activities listed in Art. R151-3 CMF—ISIC 6499 is non-sensitive, so no prior authorisation is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no surrender requirement, no mandatory repatriation timeline and no forced conversion of export proceeds into EUR. Exporters and trading companies may freely hold and use foreign currency receipts abroad or in French bank accounts, without any obligation to repatriate or convert within a statutory period. The only relevant duties are (i) statistical reporting to the Banque de France for monthly cumulative cross-border transfers of EUR 750,000 or more, filed by the account-holding bank; and (ii) customs cash declaration for physical cash movements of EUR 10,000 or more under EU Regulation 2018/1672. A private-equity buyout SPV with ISIC 6499 status has no export- surrender obligations whatsoever.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW-MEDIUM and strictly auxiliary. Fintech Electronic Money Institutions (établissements de monnaie électronique authorised by the ACPR under PSD2) may legally open payment accounts, issue e-money, execute SEPA and SWIFT transfers and issue cards. However, an EMI is not a credit institution: it cannot accept deposits, grant credit, pay interest, operate a true M&A escrow (séquestre) or participate directly in TARGET2/T2 settlement. For an ISIC 6499 leveraged buyout SPV, the EMI channel is viable only for low-value operating expenses (consultancy invoices, domiciliation fees, regulatory costs); all acquisition consideration, loan drawdowns, equity injections and intercompany funding must be held at a licensed French or EU credit institution to comply with French banking and safeguarding rules.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML law (Code monétaire et financier Arts. L561-5 to L561-22) does not statutorily compel physical appearance of directors for corporate account opening, but ACPR supervisory expectations and Tier-1 French bank policies effectively require at least one physical onboarding interview by the gérant, a co-gérant or a duly authorised signatory at the bank's commercial branch or corporate KYC office in France. For non-resident gérants, most banks accept an enhanced remote video-identification session combined with a notarised copy of the passport, a legalised/apostilled board resolution and the involvement of a French professional intermediary (avocat or corporate services provider); nonetheless, account activation may remain subject to the bank's local compliance committee approval. Fully remote opening without any interview is not practically available for a leveraged buyout SPV. The recommended mitigation is to appoint a French-resident gérant or use a recognised French law firm as the point of contact to shorten the onboarding timeline and increase approval certainty.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-tier non-resident ownership structure (Cayman/Luxembourg fund → intermediate holdco → FR SARL) rendering ultimate beneficial owners opaque; French banks classify the entity as a shell-company risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete ownership chain from each natural-person UBO to the SARL; certificate of incumbency for each intermediate entity; French RBE (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) extract; LEI certificate; group organigram; LP subscription book; notarised passport copies and proof of residential address for all UBOs; source-of-funds certification signed by the fund's general partner; and the executed SPA or term sheet proving the real economic purpose of the buyout.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sudden high-volume inbound wires (capital calls and debt drawdowns) exceeding EUR 750,000 within compressed timelines, inconsistent with the substance-light SPV profile and triggering suspicious-transaction reporting to Tracfin.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed LBO facility agreement and lender commitment letters; capital call notices; acquisition SPA and price-adjustment protocol; escrow agreement; shareholder resolutions approving the financing; lender security checklist; accounting trail evidencing that inbound funds are recorded as share capital or shareholder advances; and a transaction-specific explanatory memorandum describing the acquisition timeline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A non-resident PEP or a UBO associated with a FATF high-risk or sanctioned jurisdiction appears as an indirect limited partner, exposing the bank to EU restrictive-measures and AML reputational risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due-diligence report covering PEP status and source of wealth; UN/EU/OFAC sanctions-screening results demonstrating zero positive hits; sworn UBO declarations; independent legal opinions from a French avocat and fund counsel on the legitimate origin of funds; and, where the PEP interest cannot be fully rebutted, a proposed ring-fencing or exclusion mechanism removing the PEP-linked interest from the French holding chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient economic substance: a registered office located only at a commercial domiciliation company leads the bank to treat the SARL as a high-risk shell in line with ACPR AML doctrine.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Licensed domiciliation contract or lease; French SIREN/SIRET registration; annual accounts filed with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; designation of a French- resident gérant; staffing and professional-services agreements; opening balance sheet and business plan; shareholders' meeting minutes appointing management; and evidence that the ISIC 6499 buyout SPV actively utilises treasury, escrow and notarial services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: MT103 ordering or beneficiary references mentioning a sanctioned party or an embargoed jurisdiction, including legacy-group counterparties from high-risk regions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete KYC pack for each counterparty; sanctions-screening audit trail; narrative of purpose codes and underlying contracts; compliance certification confirming conformity with EU Regulation 833/2014 and all applicable French sanctions law, plus the French blocking statute (loi n° 68-678) where foreign evidentiary demands arise; certificates of origin and end-use for any trade-related payments; and a clear sanctions-policy remediation plan acceptable to the bank's sanctions officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity and shareholder-loan injections must be routed by SWIFT MT103 (non-EEA payer) or SEPA Credit Transfer (EEA payer) to the SARL's French IBAN (format FR76 + bank code + branch code + account number + key) with the beneficiary name exactly matching the registration and the SIREN/SIRET in the reference field. The Remittance Information field (field 70) must clearly state 'APPORT EN CAPITAL' or 'AVANCE EN COMPTE COURANT D'ASSOCIÉ'; the bank maps the narrative to the Eurosystem balance-of-payments standard purpose code for equity injection or intra-group lending. Supporting documentation required by the receiving bank: (i) executed subscription resolution (PV d'assemblée or décision du gérant); (ii) capital-increase deed or shareholder-loan agreement; (iii) up-to-date UBO/ownership chart and LEI; (iv) source-of-funds statement for the injecting fund; and (v) for a non-EU investor, evidence that the French target is not in a sensitive activity under Art. R151-3 CMF, thereby avoiding prior ministerial authorisation; the investment is then captured by the regular balance-of-payments survey transmitted by the bank to the Banque de France when the monthly cumulative cross-border flow reaches EUR 750,000. Narrative consistency with corporate documentation is decisive to prevent the bank from re-characterising the inflow as undeclared revenue or financing proceeds requiring additional scrutiny.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Acquisition consideration, including purchase price and post-closing adjustments, is disbursed by SWIFT MT103/MT202 COV from the SARL's operational or escrow account to the seller's bank; for France-to-France deliveries, settlement is made by SEPA credit transfer contemporaneously with the delivery of shares on the target's register (delivery-versus-payment). Cross-border LBO payments are typically cleared via TARGET2/T2 for EUR legs and via CLS for USD/GBP legs where the corresponding FX hedge is in place; substantial transactions may be routed through the bank's payments factory to align the MT103 cover with the syndicated facility drawdown. Documentary credits (SWIFT MT700) and standby letters of credit (MT760) are used only where portfolio-company trade flows require purchase-price support or performance guarantees, typically under URDG 758 or ISP98. No French central-bank pre-authorisation is required for ordinary disbursements; the bank will register outbound flows in the monthly French balance-of-payments survey where the cumulative amount with non-residents equals or exceeds EUR 750,000, and each payment leg is subject to real-time sanctions and PEP screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward Contracts (change à terme) - OTC, EUR/USD and EUR/GBP, governed by ISDA 1998 FX Definitions and French banking federation (AFB) master agreements, with physical delivery of EUR against the foreign currency at maturity

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) - EUR/CNY, EUR/INR and EUR/BRL style exposures, cash-settled in EUR under ISDA 1998 FX Definitions, authorised only where the underlying currency is non-convertible or subject to settlement restrictions

Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) - fixed/floating EUR-USD or EUR-GBP swaps matching LBO debt service and acquisition funding flows, documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Credit Support Annex for collateral exchange

FX Options (vanilla and barrier structures) - for acquisition-price downside protection in foreign currency, with premium charged to the operational account and settlement via physical delivery or cash settlement
FX Swaps (swap de change) - spot/forward combinations for short-term liquidity management between EUR and trade-currency balances
CLS-settled Spot FX - EUR/USD, EUR/GBP and EUR/JPY spot legs executed through the bank's single-dealer platform with Continuous Linked Settlement to eliminate settlement risk
